## Natural history notes

A medium-sized prominent moth characterized by mottled gray, brown, and whitish forewings with irregular dark lines and a bark-like pattern that helps it blend against tree trunks and dead leaves. In Florida, the Mottled Prominent is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, forest edges, parks, and wooded yards where suitable host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on hardwood foliage, especially oaks and related trees, helping transfer leaf growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
